subject: forensic-medicine
title: Trace Evidence: Forensic Bloodstain Analysis and Semen Examination

steps.title: The four fundamental questions in forensic bloodstain examination
steps.tx: When suspicious stains are encountered on weapons, clothing, or crime scene floors, forensic scientists address **four sequential bloodstain examination questions**. The laboratory must systematically prove: first, is the suspected stain genuinely blood; second, if blood, is it of human or animal origin; third, if human, what is the blood group and individual DNA profile; and fourth, what was the physical directionality and age of deposition.
steps.say: Forensic blood examination answers four questions: Is it blood, is it human, whose blood is it, and what were the angle and age of the stain?

nodes.label: Step 1: Presumptive and confirmatory tests confirm presence of blood
Step 2: Precipitin test determines human versus animal origin
Step 3: STR DNA profiling establishes individual identity
Step 4: Bloodstain pattern analysis reconstructs assault dynamics

steps.title: Presumptive catalytic tests: Benzidine and phenolphthalein
steps.tx: Initial screening relies on **presumptive catalytic screening tests**, which exploit the peroxidase-like enzymatic activity of blood hemoglobin to oxidize chemical chromogens in the presence of hydrogen peroxide. The historical benzidine test produces an intense blue color with extreme sensitivity (one in three hundred thousand), but is largely phased out due to carcinogenicity. The Kastle-Meyer phenolphthalein test provides a safe, highly sensitive alternative, producing deep pink magenta within seconds.
steps.say: Presumptive tests use hemoglobin peroxidase action to produce color changes, including the historic benzidine test and the pink Kastle-Meyer test.

rows: Highly reliable; false positives with plant peroxidases
Visualizes washed, latent bloodstains across large crime scenes
Stable reagent used on porous floorboards and fabrics

steps.title: Confirmatory microcrystalline tests: The Teichmann test
steps.tx: To confirm that a stain is blood beyond presumptive doubt, the laboratory performs **microcrystalline Teichmann haemin testing**. Discovered by Ludwik Teichmann, dried stain scrapings are placed on a glass slide, treated with a drop of glacial acetic acid containing trace sodium chloride, covered with a coverslip, and heated gently over a microflame. Under light microscopy, dark brown, rhombic, prismatic crystals of haemin (hematin hydrochloride) confirm blood.
steps.say: The Teichmann test heats blood scrapings with glacial acetic acid and salt, producing dark brown rhombic haemin crystals under the microscope.

nodes.label: Stain scraping placed on clean microscope glass slide
Addition of Teichmann reagent (glacial acetic acid + NaCl)
Gentle slow heating over spirit lamp until boiling bubbles appear
Microscopic visualization of dark brown rhombic haemin crystals

steps.tx: A stain is confirmed as blood by **microcrystalline Teichmann haemin testing**, described by Ludwik Teichmann. Scrapings go on a slide with glacial acetic acid that contains a trace of sodium chloride, a coverslip is added, and the preparation is warmed gently over a small flame. Light microscopy then shows dark brown rhombic or prismatic crystals of haemin, which is hematin hydrochloride. Those crystals carry the confirmation beyond a colour screening test.
steps.say: Dried blood scrapings heated with glacial acetic acid and a little salt form dark brown rhombic haemin crystals. Seeing those crystals under the microscope confirms that the stain is blood.

vis.alt: Dark brown rhombic crystals of haemin are seen under the light microscope from a bloodstain extract.
vis.caption: Prismatic brown haemin crystals lie on the slide after a dried stain is heated with acetic acid and salt. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: The Takayama haemochromogen crystal test
steps.tx: When stains are old, weathered, or failed under Teichmann testing, the **Takayama haemochromogen crystal test** provides the most dependable confirmatory microcrystalline technique. The reagent combines pyridine, sodium hydroxide, and glucose. Upon gentle heating, pyridine combines with reduced heme, precipitating characteristic salmon-pink, shallow rhomboid needles or wheatsheaf crystals of pyridine haemochromogen. Takayama testing is remarkably robust, functioning effectively even on decades-old washed stains.
steps.say: The Takayama test uses pyridine and glucose to form salmon-pink wheatsheaf crystals, reliably identifying blood even on very old or washed fabrics.

left.title: Teichmann test (Haemin)
points: Reagent: Glacial acetic acid with trace chloride
Forms dark brown, rhombic prismatic crystals
Extremely heat-sensitive; easily ruined by overheating
May fail on old, weathered or laundered fabrics

right.title: Takayama test (Haemochromogen)
points: Reagent: Pyridine, glucose, and sodium hydroxide
Forms flat, salmon-pink rhomboid / wheatsheaf needles
Less sensitive to thermal variation during heating
Highly dependable on old, heated, or decomposed stains

steps.tx: Old, weathered, or Teichmann negative stains are better confirmed by the **Takayama haemochromogen crystal test**. The reagent mixes pyridine, sodium hydroxide, and glucose. Gentle heat lets pyridine combine with reduced heme, and salmon pink shallow rhomboid needles or wheatsheaf crystals of pyridine haemochromogen precipitate. The reaction still works on stains washed or decades old, which is why many laboratories prefer it when the haemin test fails.
steps.say: Pyridine, alkali, and glucose heated with a doubtful stain yield salmon pink wheatsheaf crystals of haemochromogen. The Takayama result still appears on very old or washed blood.

vis.alt: Salmon pink wheatsheaf crystals of haemochromogen appear under the light microscope.
vis.caption: Shallow rhomboid needles cluster like wheat sheaves after pyridine reagent acts on an old bloodstain. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Determining human species origin: The precipitin test
steps.tx: Once blood presence is confirmed, determining whether the specimen originated from a human requires the **serological precipitin precipitin test** (Uhlenhuth test). The saline extract of the unknown stain is brought into contact with anti-human rabbit serum in a narrow capillary tube or agarose gel plate. If the stain is human, anti-human antibodies bind human serum albumin and globulins, producing a distinct cloudy white precipitation ring at the liquid interface.
steps.say: The precipitin test identifies human blood by layering stain extract against anti-human rabbit serum, creating a white precipitation ring.

nodes.label: Saline extraction of bloodstain proteins from fabric
Layering extract over anti-human rabbit antiserum in capillary tube
Incubation at room temperature for 10 to 20 minutes
Formation of white precipitate ring confirms human species

steps.title: Seminal fluid identification in sexual offences
steps.tx: In rape and sodomy investigations, detecting **forensic seminal fluid trace evidence** provides objective proof of sexual contact. Semen comprises spermatozoa suspended in seminal plasma secreted by seminal vesicles, prostate, and bulbourethral glands. Stains on victim clothing or bedding appear stiff, starchy, grayish-white with irregular map-like edges, and exhibit intense bluish-white fluorescence under ultraviolet light illumination, guiding the forensic examiner to cut targeted fabric swatches.
steps.say: Seminal stains feel stiff and starchy, showing irregular map-like edges and bright bluish fluorescence under ultraviolet light on victim clothing.

rows: Localizes suspected stain zones on dark bedding
Strong bluish-white glow under Wood lamp
Extremely high enzymatic activity (> 300 KA units)
Visualizing intact heads and flagellar tails
Absolute confirmatory physical proof of semen

steps.title: Presumptive chemical testing: Prostatic acid phosphatase
steps.tx: The standard chemical test for semen is the **prostatic acid phosphatase enzyme assay** (Walker test). The human prostate gland secretes immense concentrations of acid phosphatase into seminal fluid, exceeding concentrations in any other human tissue by hundreds of times. Treating a stain extract with alpha-naphthyl phosphate and Brentamine Fast Blue B diazotizes the released naphthol, producing an intense purple-violet coloration within thirty seconds.
steps.say: The acid phosphatase test detects prostatic enzymes in semen, producing an intense purple color within thirty seconds to confirm suspected stains.

nodes.label: Filter paper moistened with water pressed onto suspected stain
Reagent applied: Sodium alpha-naphthyl phosphate + Fast Blue B
Cleavage of phosphate releases free naphthol substrate
Instant purple-violet color within 30 seconds indicates semen

steps.title: Microscopic demonstration of spermatozoa
steps.tx: Providing absolute legal confirmation of seminal contact, the **microscopic spermatozoa cytological demonstration** visualizes male gametes directly under light microscopy. Smears prepared from vaginal swabs or stained clothing are stained with Christmas tree stain (Picroindigocarmine and Nuclear Fast Red). The oval sperm head stains bright red or pink with a lighter anterior acrosome cap, while the intermediate neck and flagellar tail stain vibrant green.
steps.say: Christmas tree staining provides conclusive proof of semen, coloring sperm heads bright red and flagellar tails green under high-power microscopy.

nodes.label: Elution of seminal swab in sterile distilled water
Centrifugation to concentrate cellular sediment pellet
Smear staining with Nuclear Fast Red and Picroindigocarmine
Visualization of red sperm heads and green tails at 400x

steps.tx: Absolute proof of seminal contact is the **microscopic spermatozoa cytological demonstration** of male gametes on a smear. Vaginal swabs or stained cloth are coloured with Christmas tree stain, picroindigocarmine and nuclear fast red. The oval head becomes bright red or pink, with a paler acrosome at the front, while the neck and tail turn green. Seeing that red and green gamete is stronger evidence than chemical crystal tests alone.
steps.say: Christmas tree stain colours the sperm head red or pink, with a lighter acrosome, and the neck and tail green. Finding those cells on a swab or cloth proves semen more certainly than crystal tests.

vis.alt: Stained spermatozoa under the microscope show distinct heads and tails.
vis.caption: Oval sperm heads take a red stain and the necks and tails take green on a Christmas tree preparation. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Semen detection in azoospermic or vasectomized subjects
steps.tx: When an assailant is vasectomized, azoospermic, or oligospermic, intact spermatozoa are completely absent, rendering microscopic searches negative. Under these circumstances, forensic laboratories deploy **prostate-specific antigen p30 immunochromatography**. PSA is a glycoprotein produced by prostatic epithelial cells, independent of spermatogenesis. Detection of p30 using rapid lateral flow immunochromatographic strips confirms human semen beyond doubt, enabling subsequent male epithelial DNA profiling.
steps.say: In vasectomized or azoospermic men, semen lacks sperm, so labs detect prostate-specific antigen p30 using rapid lateral flow test strips.

left.title: Sperm-positive seminal stain
points: Contains intact spermatozoa with heads and tails
Confirmed by Christmas tree differential staining
Nuclear DNA easily extracted from sperm heads
Typical of normal fertile post-pubertal males

right.title: Azoospermic / vasectomized stain
points: Completely devoid of spermatozoa on microscopy
Acid phosphatase test remains strongly positive
Male identity established from seminal epithelial cells
